key_insight: High-rate cavitation reveals effective viscosity reductions across tested soft materials, while shear modulus reductions vary by material and formulation and can occur at different stages.
engineering_relevance: Time-varying property estimates can improve characterization of tissue-like materials subjected to rapid loading in biomechanics and medical engineering.
method: Infer viscoelastic properties from laser-induced bubble radius–time histories using Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry.
Represent evolving shear modulus, viscosity, or both with normalized sigmoid histories.
Validate on synthetic histories and apply to polyacrylamide and gelatin datasets.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests recovered prescribed constant and time-varying histories; experimental datasets showed viscosity decreases and formulation-dependent shear modulus reductions.
watch_item: The inferred histories are effective properties constrained by sigmoid parameterizations, not direct evidence distinguishing damage, fracture, and plasticity.
paper_title: Soft material mechanical property degradation at high strain rates
